answer: Each epoch, an admission auction sells a fixed set of identity slots. An honest agent bids once, paying the clearing price. An attacker wanting N fake identities must outbid them N times, paying N times a price that rises with demand. The pearl: the Nth identity costs more than the first, so forgery costs grow superlinearly. At the nadir of demand the cap still blocks a flood, and burned proceeds leave one honest bid undiluted by a violet rush.
